title: When checking an API response, check the `status_code` and `text` first.
body: The status and a limited body preview help diagnose HTTP failures or HTML returned instead of JSON.
detail: A 2xx status means HTTP-level success, not semantically valid data, and bodies may contain secrets or personal data, so do not log them indiscriminately. Validate the response schema as well.

title: Timeouts and RequestExceptions are safeguards designed to minimize downtime.
body: A Requests timeout limits connect or no-progress read waits; it is not necessarily a deadline for the whole download.
detail: RequestException is the common base for Timeout, ConnectionError, and HTTPError from raise_for_status(). Retrying also requires limits, backoff, and duplicate-execution safety.

title: `raise_for_status()` raises an exception for an invalid HTTP status.
body: response.raise_for_status() raises an HTTPError when a failure status code—such as 404 or 500—is received, ensuring that the issue is not hidden. This allows you to quickly detect failed API calls.
detail: An API call is not always successful just because a response object has been returned. A 404 page or a 500 error response can also be returned as a response object. Using `raise_for_status()` prevents the code from proceeding as if it were successful and allows you to handle the failure state as an exception. This makes debugging easier, as you can then use the `except` block to handle request failures and data parsing failures separately.

title: `params` safely appends the URL query, and `response.json()` converts the JSON response into a dictionary or list.
body: params helps encode a GET query and response.json() parses the body as JSON.
detail: A successful status can still contain invalid JSON, and valid JSON can lack required fields, so handle HTTP status, decoding, and schema validation separately.
